title: Cloud Posture Findings Baseline

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay or inject sample `aws:securityhub:findings` events matching `*` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.10.1 search returns >=1 row and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:securityhub:findings` traffic without `*` markers. Confirm the search returns zero rows and alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:securityhub:findings` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS (Splunkbase 1876); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: Verifies cloud posture findings baseline data flows into Splunk continuously. This UC monitors `aws:securityhub:findings` for cloud posture findings baseline and surfaces events for SOC triage, change review, and compliance evidence.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (Splunkbase 1876) with the modular input for `aws:securityhub:findings`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): none.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `Finding.Title` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable aws:securityhub:findings ingestion via the appropriate Splunk TA into index=aws.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:securityhub:findings" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:securityhub:findings"
| table _time Finding.Title Finding.Severity.Label Finding.AwsAccountId
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.10.1_cloud_posture_findings_b_1"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:securityhub:findings` in `index=aws` to detect cloud posture findings baseline. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS Security Hub console Findings for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `Finding.Title` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_10_1_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Ingestion health single value and lag chart..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (Splunkbase 1876) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud posture findings baseline so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
